purpose: Distinguish whether the learned PM adds benefit, avoids unnecessary resources, beats transparent rules, and selects better than an amount-matched nonsemantic policy without mixing policy and memory-representation comparisons.

directly_reusable: baseline research questions and domain applicability
official-aligned Token F1 and frozen BERTScore definitions
Raw Session Top-4 and All Raw Sessions as EvoEmo representation baselines
same-state alias deduplication and logical-arm retention
must_be_rematerialized_or_rerun: all response baseline prompts and generations under V5.3 typed whole-response Step2
all V5.3 candidate snapshots, actual Rank-1 identities, actions, seeds, token accounting, and evaluator packets
all raw-session response baselines on the final 204-state EvoEmo panel
historical_only_unless_exact_current_sta: V5.1/V5.2 response quality and risk scores
reuse_decision.reason: V5.3 changes the training target and response executor; old outcomes combine different states, compilers, prompts, generators, and evidence-integration semantics.

conditions.question: Does learned routing create conditional benefit relative to injecting no optional resource?
Can learned routing preserve quality/risk while using less context than an always-use-available-resources system?
Does learned conditional value add anything beyond a simple auditable heuristic?

conditions.action: OOF/cross-fitted predictions from formally passing heads; every failed or state-level abstaining head is fixed OFF; transparent_rule is a separate baseline and is never substituted inside this arm
conditions.question: What does the deployable V5.3 PM do?

conditions.action: one outcome-blind fixed action per preregistered broad stratum, selected only to approximate learned deterministic injected-token cost
conditions.question: Could a static resource bundle at similar cost explain the result?

conditions.action: outcome-blind constrained permutation of learned action bundles within exchangeable cells
conditions.question: Is semantic state-to-action matching better than using the same amount and component frequency at random?
conditions.role: strongest selection-specific comparator subject to qualification

qualified_policy_naming.learned_pm_full_allowed: only when all four formal heads pass; then it is an alias of learned_pm_qualified
qualified_policy_naming.partial_head_case: the main deployable arm remains learned_pm_qualified and failed heads are visibly fixed OFF; an unqualified all-head arm is not a main baseline
qualified_policy_naming.transparent_rule_separation: transparent_rule remains an independent logical arm; it cannot repair or replace a failed learned head

same_stack_invariants: same candidate discovery and actual Rank-1
response_core.physical_alias_rule: Identical state, action, evidence material, and seed generate once; all logical policy aliases remain in the analysis table and alias rates are reported.

cost_matched_fixed.stratum_rule: domain plus preregistered broad opportunity stratum; no stratum may be defined from response/evaluation outcomes
cost_matched_fixed.candidate_actions: all 16 actions projected through the state's eligible mask
cost_matched_fixed.selection: choose the single fixed action whose mean deterministic incremental injected-prompt tokens are closest to learned_pm_qualified; stable protocol hash breaks ties
cost_matched_fixed.qualification: absolute relative deterministic-cost mismatch at most 5 percent; otherwise name/report closest-cost-fixed and do not claim a cost-matched comparison

cost_and_on_rate_matched_random.exchangeability_cell: domain/broad stratum plus exact eligible mask; token length is not an exact cell key
cost_and_on_rate_matched_random.assignment: permute learned action bundles only within cells, preserving the component action distribution exactly; among outcome-blind protocol-hash candidate permutations choose the one minimizing deterministic injected-token cost mismatch
qualification: component ON counts exactly equal learned within the full panel
total deterministic incremental injected-prompt-token mismatch at most 5 percent
at least 25 percent of states receive a different action than learned
no response, Q, risk, judge, or external outcome is used
cost_and_on_rate_matched_random.failure: if qualification fails, report the alias/mismatch and omit superiority language against this arm; never keep the name matched-random for an effectively identical policy

ESConv_response.mask: MP/MS/ME unavailable; comparisons reduce to the RS bit
ESConv_response.alias_handling: retain logical arms, deduplicate identical physical calls, and report when fixed/cost-matched arms collapse to always_off or fixed_high

secondary_mechanism: 16-action oracle upper bound on the separate interaction panel

not_applicable: response transparent_rule as a main QA comparator

representation_baseline_boundary.raw_session_top4_and_full_history: secondary system/representation comparisons, not legal PM actions and not evidence that policy routing alone caused a difference
representation_baseline_boundary.same_requirements: same source user, strictly-past cutoff, current query, generator endpoint, seed, output cap, and evaluator
representation_baseline_boundary.allowed_difference: the predeclared memory representation/retrieval method and resulting context only

legacy_boundary.V1_0: historical context only unless exact current-stack replay is possible; raw-session questions are already covered by current-stack raw baselines
legacy_boundary.V5_2_append: architecture-failure historical ablation, not a main PM baseline; old scores cannot be pooled with V5.3
legacy_boundary.current_stack_replay: must use the final V5.3 states, candidate identities, generator, seeds, evaluator, and a clearly named altered-executor system ablation

per_comparison: logical and unique physical call counts
deterministic planned and realized provider token costs
material risk difference and critical events

no_feedback_rule: Baseline definitions, matching tolerance, exchangeability cells, alias rules, and domain applicability cannot change after V5.3 response or QA outcomes are opened.
